top/setup: Here is a forward pass, already run. The hidden layer, h, is two and zero: the second unit's pre-activation was minus one, so the ReLU zeroed it. The scores came out three and three.
top/ds: The loss sends back its gradient on the scores, ds. With class zero correct, softmax gives minus a half and a half.
top/dW2: The second layer computes W two times h. As for any matrix product, the gradient on W two is ds times h transposed: entry i, j is ds i, times h j.
top/entries: Row zero: minus a half times two is minus one, and times zero is zero. Row one: one, and zero. The weights that read the silent unit get nothing.
top/db2: The bias adds straight onto the scores, so its gradient is ds itself: minus a half, and a half.
down/dh: To keep going, we need the gradient on h. It is W two transposed, times ds: each hidden unit collects the gradient of every score it fed, weighted by the weight it fed it through.
down/u0: Unit zero fed score zero with weight one, and score one with weight two. One times minus a half, plus two times a half, is a half.
down/u1: Unit one, with weights minus one and one: a half, plus a half, is one.
mask/mask: Now the ReLU. Its slope is one where its input was positive and zero where it was negative. So the gradient passes where a unit was on, and stops where it was off.
mask/apply: Unit zero was on, so it keeps its half. Unit one was off, so its gradient of one becomes zero.
mask/dW1: From here, the first layer works like the second: the gradient on W one is that masked gradient times x transposed. The off unit's row is all zeros: from this example, no gradient reaches its weights at all.
